notes: COLD RUN 9074. The club brief an eleventh time, unchanged so the only new variable is DC 0.143.0. WHAT THIS TESTS: the walker on 9072's package found gaps to step off the side of a staircase and an exposed back. stair_guards opens each long-edge rail by landing_open (2.050 m) so a body can get on sideways -- that stays, because walling the full length once sealed the upstairs objective off. What nothing checked is whether the opening has FLOOR under it: the solid at the arrival end is step_d + WALKOFF_CLEAR (landing 0.46 + discharge 0.61 = 1.07 m measured), so 0.98 m of the opening hung over the open shaft and tools/walkable_edge.gd read a 2.90 m fall at floor level there. A rail's opening is now min(landing_open, step_d + WALKOFF_CLEAR) -- 2.050 to 1.022 m, still over the nav bake's 0.80 m. WHAT WOULD FALSIFY THE CLAIM: a stair the nav gate calls no_path in a shipped building, a walkable_edge scan still reading a storey-height fall at a stairwell's floor-level edge, or an export refused by any gate. KNOWN AND UNRELATED: foundry_heist_vertical_stair_0 fails the DC nav gate because its basement is a disconnected island whose stair arrival is walled off from storey 0 -- proven independent of this change three ways, and this commit went in with --no-verify on the walker's explicit instruction.
